- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes unrealistically; cap forecasts at 1.5x recent low or 1.2x recent mean.
- After sharp spikes in forecast (e.g., >5x recent mean), apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce by 50% of spike magnitude for next 3–5 days.
- If forecast mean is >2.5x true mean over 30d, apply mean reversion: force forecast to align with 70% of 30d true mean unless sentiment strongly supports upside.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model often misreads trend direction; use sentiment momentum: if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ days, forecast should trend up; if <0.33 for 3+ days, forecast should trend down.
- Avoid forecasting >3x recent high unless sentiment is >0.80 and stable; otherwise, cap at 2x recent high to prevent over-optimism.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after forecast spike, assume model overreacted; apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.2–0.5 from forecast for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
